name: Measure Pseudopartitive with Of
pattern: NP[quantified measure expression + of + substance or plural nominal expression]

entry.name: Measure Pseudopartitive with Of
entry.pattern: NP[quantified measure expression + of + substance or plural nominal expression]

1.definition: Uses a unit or container expression to specify quantity.

examples.form: They bought [three litres of the milk from yesterday].
examples.note: Constructed comparison. The construction can instead pick a quantity out of an established stock.

projection.target: Milk supplies the substance measured without referring to a definite stock of which the purchase was a subset. Compare three litres of the milk, which can select from such a stock.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Amounts and containers followed by of
curious.summary: A unit or container word followed by of says how much of a substance or how many things were involved.
curious.body:
In They bought three litres of milk, three litres says how much milk. The milk isn't a particular stock of milk the shopper chose from. It's just the substance being measured.

Compare They bought three litres of the milk from yesterday. Here the speaker picks a quantity out of an established stock: the milk from yesterday. Adding the changes the meaning from measuring a substance to selecting from one already known.

examples.text: They bought [three litres of the milk from yesterday].

curious.try: Say three litres of milk, then three litres of the milk. Which one points to milk you've already been talking about?

teacher.summary: Helps explain three litres of milk, where a unit or container word measures a substance, and how it differs from picking out part of a known stock.
teacher.explain: A measure pseudopartitive uses a unit or container expression plus of to specify quantity: three litres of milk. The milk supplies the substance measured and doesn't refer to a definite stock of which the purchase was a subset. Compare three litres of the milk from yesterday, which can select from such a stock. The pattern takes a substance or a plural nominal after of. This dictionary treats it as a kind of noun phrase and relates it to the measurement adjective pattern (six feet long).
teacher.terms: Pseudopartitive is the textbook name. A true partitive, as in two of the cats, selects from an established stock, and the measure pseudopartitive does not.

contrasts.text: They bought three litres of milk.
They bought three litres of the milk from yesterday.
contrasts.note: Can instead pick a quantity out of an established stock.

watch_for: A learner might read three litres of milk as a portion of milk already mentioned, when it measures the substance.
A learner might think adding the changes only the wording, when it can shift the sense from measuring to selecting.
teacher.activity: Give students unit and container words, such as litres, bags and cups, with substances and plural nouns. They build sentences with of, then add the plus a definite phrase to one of them and explain what changed.

child.hook: How do you say how much milk you want?
child.explain: You can name an amount or a container, then say of, then say what it holds. Three litres of milk. The word of links the amount to the stuff.
child.play: Look in the kitchen. Name a container or a measure, then say of and what is inside. Make three sentences, like a bag of apples or a cup of tea.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Measure Pseudopartitive with Of." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/measure-pseudopartitive-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
